candidates.title: Bone health, obesity, and multimorbidity risk among teachers in under-resourced South African public primary schools: results from a cross-sectional DXA study.
candidates.abstract: In low- and middle-income countries, adverse body composition risk is increasingly driven by structural determinants, including rapid urbanisation, nutrition transitions, and reduced opportunities for physical activity. Quantifying and interpreting bone, fat and lean mass risks require appropriate measurement and context-sensitive thresholds to detect subclinical vulnerability in under-resourced settings. Few studies, particularly from Africa, have quantified how these risks intersect and cluster with cardiometabolic and socio-demographic determinants. The purpose of this study was to characterise body composition profiles, estimate the prevalence and co-occurrence of risk phenotypes and examine their distribution across health determinants. The study was carried out in under-resourced public schools in Gqeberha, Eastern Cape, South Africa, as part of the KaziBantu project (ISRCTN18485542). A school-based workplace health intervention was conducted, using cross-sectional assessments. We employed dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), assessed metabolic indicators, behavioural indicators (alcohol and tobacco use, device-measured physical activity, handgrip strength), and obtained demographic and medical data. Among 136 apparently healthy teachers (85% women; age 21-72 years; mean = 47 years; standard deviation = 11 years), body composition risk was prevalent: fat mass risk 91.8% (n = 123/134; 95%CI 85.8-95.8%), lean mass risk 15.7% (n = 21/134; 95%CI 10-23%) and bone mass risk 29.9% (n = 40/134; 95%CI 22.3-38.4%). The most frequent combined phenotype was bone-fat risk (27.6%; n = 37; 95%CI 20.2-36%), while 6% (n = 8; 95%CI 2.6-11.4%) exhibited all three risks concurrently. Metabolic syndrome criteria were met in 53% (n = 70; 95%CI 44.2-61.8%) of teachers, and adverse risk phenotypes were associated with elevated multimorbidity and poorer metabolic health. This is the first study from South Africa's Eastern Cape to report DXA-derived body composition profiles. Body composition risks and multimorbidity were prevalent, with likely substantial impacts on quality of life. Protecting teachers' health will require multi-level strategies, including workplace-based screening with low-cost tools (e.g., bioelectrical impedance), culturally responsive prevention such as targeted weight-bearing and resistance activity, and action on structural inequities, such as more equitable resourcing across schools to reduce occupational strain and stronger pathways that turn teachers' existing health coverage into timely screening and treatment. These strategies aim to safeguard well-being and sustain teachers' pivotal role in educating future generations.

candidates.title: The Effect of Digital Storytelling on the Anxiety of Patients with Pituitary Adenoma Undergoing Transsphenoidal Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial.
candidates.abstract: Patients with pituitary adenoma often experience anxiety due to hormonal changes and the stress associated with transsphenoidal surgery. Digital storytelling, as an innovative multimedia-based training method, has recently been used in patient education. This study investigated the effect of digital storytelling on the anxiety of patients with pituitary adenoma undergoing transsphenoidal surgery. This randomized controlled trial was conducted on 70 patients with pituitary adenoma scheduled for transsphenoidal surgery at a teaching hospital affiliated with Tehran University of Medical Sciences. Participants were randomly assigned to an intervention or a control group. The intervention group received a 15-20-minute digital storytelling program that included experiences shared by patients and nurses regarding preoperative and postoperative care, while the control group received routine hospital education. Anxiety levels were measured a day before surgery, a day after surgery, and three weeks later using Spielberger's State Anxiety Scale. Data were analyzed by SPSS-25 software using descriptive and inferential statistics. The mean score of anxiety in the intervention group decreased by 12.45 (1.24) units a day after the surgery and by 24.82 (1.32) units three weeks after the surgery compared to baseline (p < 0.001). A significantly lower anxiety level was observed in the intervention group at both post-intervention time periods compared to the pre-intervention time (F = 17.05, p < 0.001). Repeated measures Analysis of Variance confirmed a significant interaction between time and group (F = 25.31, p < 0.001). Digital storytelling was effective in reducing anxiety among patients with pituitary adenoma undergoing transsphenoidal surgery and may serve as a valuable educational intervention.

candidates.title: Acinetobacter baumannii Nosocomial Meningitis Secondary to Neurosurgical Intervention: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Nosocomial meningitis is a serious complication of neurosurgical procedures, associated with high morbidity and mortality, as well as significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Among the causative pathogens, Acinetobacter baumannii (A. baumannii) is particularly concerning due to its ability to survive for prolonged periods in the hospital environment, its opportunistic virulence, and, especially, its tendency to develop multidrug resistance to antimicrobial agents. Diagnosis is often difficult in the postoperative setting, particularly when the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is altered as a result of the surgical procedure. Rapid identification of the causative agent and early initiation of appropriate antibiotic therapy are essential to limit complications and improve patient prognosis. We report the case of a 27-year-old patient with a history of surgically treated craniopharyngioma complicated by anterior hypopituitarism. Three weeks after surgery, he was admitted to the ICU with suspected postoperative meningitis due to the onset of behavioral disturbances associated with nasal discharge, without a fever. Brain CT was normal. CSF analysis, obtained by lumbar puncture under strict aseptic conditions, revealed a turbid fluid with leukocytosis of 5,760 cells/mm³, predominantly composed of neutrophils, along with elevated protein levels (5.7 g/L) and low glucose levels (0.05 g/L). Direct examination after Gram staining showed Gram-negative coccobacilli with a marked inflammatory reaction. CSF culture grew a multidrug-resistant (MDR) strain of A. baumannii, which was sensitive only to colistin. The patient received antibiotic therapy with colistin, administered intravenously and intrathecally for 18 days, with initial neurological improvement and sterilization of the CSF by the 15th day of treatment. The subsequent course was unfavorable, marked by the development of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) secondary to ventilator-associated pneumonia caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), complicated by refractory septic shock, which ultimately led to his death after one month of hospitalization in the ICU. This report highlights the severity of nosocomial meningitis caused by MDR A. baumannii and underscores the importance of implementing infection prevention measures in healthcare settings.

candidates.title: A Case of MEN 2A Syndrome With Bilateral Recurrent Pheochromocytoma: A Case Report and Literature Review.
candidates.abstract: Pheochromocytoma is a neuroendocrine tumor arising from chromaffin cells and producing catecholamines. Due to the excessive release of catecholamines, these tumors can present with paroxysmal episodes of high blood pressure, headache, diaphoresis, and palpitations. We present the case of a 23-year-old female patient who presented to the clinic with a history of headache, palpitations, and vomiting for two months. She was admitted for further investigations and management. Laboratory studies revealed elevated urinary and plasma catecholamine levels. Further work-up revealed bilateral adrenal masses diagnosed as pheochromocytoma and medullary thyroid cancer. The patient was diagnosed with multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN) type 2 and underwent bilateral laparoscopic adrenalectomy and total thyroidectomy with central and lateral neck dissection, and during surveillance, she was found to have recurrent pheochromocytoma. We also discuss the diagnosis and management of recurrent pheochromocytoma in MEN syndrome.

candidates.title: Imaging features of pituitary Crooke cell adenoma: a 13-case series.
candidates.abstract: Crooke cell adenoma (CCA) is a rare and aggressive subtype of pituitary neuroendocrine tumor (PitNET). This study aimed to characterize the imaging features of CCA. Preoperative and postoperative follow-up MR images of 13 patients with CCA were retrospectively reviewed to characterize their imaging features in conjunction with clinical and pathological findings. Among the 13 CCAs, 8 (61.5%) were macroadenomas and 5 (38.5%) were microadenomas. On T1-weighted imaging, 12 tumors (92.3%) were isointense. On T2-weighted imaging, 6 (46.2%) were hyperintense, 4 (30.8%) were hypointense, and 3 (23.1%) were isointense. Macroadenomas were predominantly hyperintense (5/8) or isointense (3/8), whereas microadenomas were predominantly hypointense (4/5). Multiple microcystic changes were observed in 2 macroadenomas (15.4%). Mild contrast enhancement was observed in 10 tumors (76.9%). Knosp grade 1 was the most common pattern of parasellar extension (8/13, 61.5%). During postoperative follow-up of 2-39 months, tumor progression occurred in 4 patients (30.8%), all of whom had undergone subtotal resection. Retrospective review of their preoperative contrast-enhanced MRI showed reduced enhancement of the tumor-adjacent internal carotid artery wall (ICAW) in all four cases. CCA exhibits several imaging characteristics, particularly mild contrast enhancement and a tumor size-related T2-weighted signal pattern. Knosp grade 1 was the most frequent parasellar extension pattern. Reduced enhancement of the tumor-adjacent ICAW was observed in four cases with postoperative tumor progression; however, the clinical significance of this finding requires validation in larger cohorts with longer-term follow-up.

candidates.title: Antimicrobial activity of ginsenoside Rh2 against Enterococcus faecalis and its biofilm.
candidates.abstract: Enterococcus faecalis (E. faecalis) is frequently associated with persistent root canal infections and treatment failure, and effective strategies for its elimination remain limited. Plant-derived compounds may provide alternative antimicrobial strategies for endodontic treatment. In the present study, we evaluated the antimicrobial activity of 20(S)-ginsenoside Rh2 (Rh2), a bioactive compound derived from ginseng, against planktonic and biofilm forms of E. faecalis. The effects of Rh2 on extracellular polysaccharide (EPS)-associated carbohydrate content and biofilm metabolic activity were evaluated using the phenol-sulfuric acid and MTT assays, respectively. Biofilm structural alterations were examined by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM). The cytotoxicity of Rh2 toward L929 cells was assessed using an MTT assay, with sodium hypochlorite (NaClO) serving as the reference antimicrobial agent. Rh2 exhibited antibacterial activity against planktonic E. faecalis, with a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 3.125 μg/mL and a minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) of 6.250 μg/mL. Rh2 inhibited biofilm formation and reduced the biomass of established biofilms at 2 × MIC and 4 × MIC. Rh2 also markedly reduced EPS-associated carbohydrate content, altered biofilm architecture, and decreased the metabolic activity of biofilm-associated bacteria. Under the tested conditions, Rh2 exhibited favorable cellular compatibility at concentrations with antibacterial activity against E. faecalis. These findings demonstrate the in vitro antibacterial and antibiofilm activities of Rh2 against E. faecalis and support further investigation of its potential as an intracanal antimicrobial agent.

candidates.title: Sinonasal and Olfactory Quality of Life Following Endonasal Transsphenoidal Surgery for Pituitary Adenoma: A Multicenter Prospective Cohort Triphasic Recovery Analysis in Ethiopia.
candidates.abstract: To characterize the sinonasal and olfactory quality of life (QoL) trajectory. A multicenter prospective cohort study was conducted on 91 patients undergoing TSS at Addis Ababa University teaching hospitals between May 2024 and August 2025. QoL was evaluated using the Sino-Nasal Outcome Test (SNOT-22) questionnaire v4 preoperatively and at 3- and 6-month postoperatively. Analysis revealed a characteristic triphasic recovery pattern: low preoperative baseline, a transient peak in morbidity at 3 months, and an improvement toward baseline by 6 months for most systemic domains. At 3 months, significant score worsening occurred for loss of smell/taste (mean: 1.7, p < 0.001), thick discharge (mean: 1.0, p < 0.001), congestion (mean: 1.0, p < 0.001), postnasal discharge (mean: 0.7, p < 0.001), and runny nose (mean: 0.5, p = 0.003). By 6 months, persistence was confined to loss of smell/taste (p < 0.001), thick discharge (p < 0.001), and congestion (p = 0.005). Exploratory analysis in the nasoseptal flap cohort (n = 3) showed higher scores. Preliminary findings of delayed ear pain/fullness in acromegaly at 6 months hypothesized to reflect a link between growth hormone normalization and altered Eustachian tube function. Poorer sleep with binostril access (p = 0.017) speculatively associated with bilateral synechiae under limited postoperative care. Unlike Western cohorts, protracted recovery may reflect lack of standardized high-volume saline irrigation and scheduled debridement. TSS demonstrates a favorable long-term QoL profile; however, localized sinonasal and olfactory deficits often persist at 6 months.

candidates.title: Newly Diagnosed Graves' Disease Followed by the Discovery of a Cavernous Internal Carotid Artery Aneurysm Causing Panhypopituitarism: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Sellar and parasellar vascular lesions are rare causes of pituitary dysfunction and may mimic pituitary adenomas or other sellar masses. Cavernous internal carotid artery (ICA) aneurysms can cause hypopituitarism through compression of the pituitary gland or stalk, but diagnosis may be delayed when symptoms are initially attributed to a more common endocrine disorder. We report a 37-year-old man who presented with six weeks of unintentional weight loss, fatigue, heat intolerance, excessive sweating, anxiety, tremor, and tachycardia. Initial evaluation showed suppressed thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), elevated total triiodothyronine (T3), positive thyrotropin receptor antibody, positive thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin, and a hypervascular thyroid gland on ultrasound, consistent with Graves' disease. He was started on methimazole and atenolol. Although thyroid function tests improved, he developed persistent neck discomfort, prompting contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT), which revealed an enhancing sellar mass. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed a T2-hypointense sellar lesion with internal flow artifact, and CT angiography confirmed a saccular aneurysm of the cavernous segment of the right ICA. Pituitary hormone evaluation demonstrated secondary adrenal insufficiency, central hypothyroidism, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, growth hormone (GH) deficiency, and mild hyperprolactinemia, consistent with panhypopituitarism from pituitary compression. The patient was started on prednisone and levothyroxine, and atenolol and prednisone were subsequently discontinued before endovascular embolization was performed. At follow-up, symptoms improved, but panhypopituitarism persisted. This case highlights the importance of reassessing patients when endocrine symptoms evolve despite an initially appropriate diagnosis.

candidates.title: Neuroendocrine dysfunction after TBI: A guide for the clinical neuropsychologist.
candidates.abstract: This review aims to provide neuropsychologists with a comprehensive understanding of neuroendocrine dysfunction following traumatic brain injury (TBI), emphasizing post-traumatic hypopituitarism (PTHP) and its implications for cognitive function and rehabilitation. A critical review of current literature on neuroendocrine dysfunction following TBI, including studies on pituitary function, hormone deficiencies, and their effects on cognition, mood, and fatigue. The review integrates findings from endocrinology, neuroscience, and clinical neuropsychology to highlight the importance of interdisciplinary management. Research indicates that a high proportion of moderate to severe TBI cases may develop PTHP, with growth hormone deficiency (GHD) as the most prevalent dysfunction. While less extensively studied, evidence suggests that individuals with persistent post-mild TBI symptoms may exhibit neuroendocrine dysfunction at similar rates to moderate to severe TBI patients. The impact of hormonal dysregulation on cognition and neuropsychological performance underscores the need for targeted assessment and intervention. Emerging data also suggest that metabolic disturbances, such as altered gut microbiota and amino acid imbalances, may contribute to post-TBI fatigue and cognitive impairment. Neuropsychologists play a vital role in identifying and referring patients with suspected neuroendocrine dysfunction for appropriate testing and treatment. Recognizing PTHP as a potential contributor to chronic TBI symptoms may lead to improved patient outcomes through targeted hormonal therapies and interdisciplinary rehabilitation strategies. Increased awareness of the relationship between TBI, pituitary dysfunction, and cognition is essential for optimizing clinical care.

candidates.title: Encapsulation of Peppermint Essential Oil (Mentha piperita L.) in Gelatin-Coated Solid Lipid Nanocarriers (PEO-SLNs): Characterization and Its Effect on Microbial Quality of Trout Fillet (Oncorhynchus mykiss).
candidates.abstract: The primary objective of this work was to develop peppermint essential oil-loaded solid lipid nanoparticles (PEO-SLNs) and evaluate their effectiveness on microbial quality of trout fillets. PEO-SLNs were prepared by bath sonication and characterized using dynamic light scattering (DLS), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR). The optimized nanoparticles exhibited a zeta potential of -21.84 ± 2.25 mV, a mean particle size of 124.18 ± 0.22 nm, and a polydispersity index (PDI) of 0.20 ± 0.02. Trout fillets were randomly assigned to four treatment groups: Group 1, uncoated fillets; Group 2, fillet coated with 5% fish gelatin; Group 3, fillets coated with 5% fish gelatin containing 0.2% PEO; and Group 4, fillets coated with 5% fish gelatin containing 0.2% PEO-SLNs. The treated fillets were stored at 4°C ± 1°C for 12 days, and microbiological analysis were performed throughout the storage. The highest reduction rates of total viable bacteria (1.20 log CFU/g), total psychrophilic bacteria (1.04 log CFU/g), Pseudomonas spp. (0.74 log CFU/g), Enterobacteriaceae (0.93 log CFU/g), Shewanella putrefaciens (0.73 log CFU/g), yeast and mold count (0.91 log CFU/g) were observed in the samples treated with gelatin-loaded SLNs containing PEO. PEO-SLNs demonstrated the highest overall microbial reduction, with statistically significant improvements compared with free PEO for four of the six evaluated microbial indicators. However, no significant difference was observed for Shewanella putrefaciens and Enterobacteriaceae. In addition, encapsulation of PEO in SLNs resulted in greater antibacterial activity than free PEO. These findings demonstrate that fish gelatin coatings incorporating PEO-SLNs represent a promising natural preservation strategy for improving the microbial quality of trout fillets.

candidates.title: Common peroneal nerve entrapment in an adolescent during a growth spurt: a case report and hypothesis on growth-related vulnerability.
candidates.abstract: Common peroneal nerve entrapment at the fibular neck is a well-recognized cause of foot drop, but atraumatic cases in adolescents may be diagnostically challenging. Rapid growth during adolescence may increase local nerve vulnerability through growth-related neuro-musculoskeletal factors, although direct evidence remains limited. We report a 16-year-old male who presented with a two-week history of weakness in the left ankle and hallux dorsiflexion without a clear history of trauma, habitual leg crossing, prolonged squatting, tight footwear, systemic disease, or family history of hereditary neuropathy. He had experienced a rapid growth period over the preceding six months, with an increase in height of approximately 6 cm and one shoe size. Physical examination revealed marked weakness of ankle and hallux dorsiflexion, sensory reduction over the lateral leg and dorsum of the foot, and a positive Tinel sign at the fibular neck. High-resolution ultrasonography demonstrated focal enlargement of the left common peroneal nerve at the fibular neck, and electrodiagnostic testing-including fibrillation potentials, motor unit action potentials (MUAPs), and reduced recruitment on needle electromyography of the tibialis anterior-was compatible with focal common peroneal neuropathy. Conservative treatment was unsuccessful. Surgical exploration revealed a discrete, tendon-like fibrous band compressing the nerve at the lower fibular neck; after division of the band, the nerve was fully decompressed. At 14 days postoperatively, dorsiflexion strength and sensory symptoms had improved, and at 3 months, the patient's mother reported continued improvement. This case suggests that common peroneal nerve entrapment should be considered in adolescents with atraumatic foot drop; a recent growth spurt may be a potential predisposing factor, although causality cannot be established. Ultrasonography and electrodiagnostic testing may help localize the lesion. Surgical decompression may be effective when symptoms are severe or conservative treatment fails. Because the proposed growth-related vulnerability is inferred from a temporal association in a single case, this report is intended to generate-rather than to prove-a clinically relevant hypothesis that warrants testing in larger, prospective series.

candidates.title: The evolution of direct transcranial photobiomodulation: a history of dose, depth, and delivery.
candidates.abstract: Direct transcranial photobiomodulation (dtPBM) delivers red or near-infrared light through the scalp and skull with the aim of affecting brain tissue. The field has produced encouraging findings but inconsistent clinical results. We reconstruct its development as a history of scientific and engineering decisions in which optical access, target depth, and dose repeatedly shaped what could be tested. The clinical lineage began with light therapy for ischemic myocardium and moved to stroke, where cadaver measurements established that near-infrared light could traverse the human scalp and skull and defined a historical design target of approximately 7.5 mW/cm2 at the dura. The NEST clinical program then carried a fixed 808-nm regimen into three stroke trials: NEST-1 met its primary endpoint, NEST-2 showed a nonsignificant overall trend (p = 0.094) with a published post hoc signal in moderate stroke (p = 0.044), and NEST-3 stopped for futility. An unpublished, exploratory NEST-2 reanalysis described larger treatment differences for superficial lesions; this observation motivates prospective testing but does not establish depth-dependent efficacy. After NEST, treatment moved to the forehead, where target geometry was more reproducible. The ELATED trials adopted a more practical LED platform at substantially lower irradiance while preserving broadly similar treatment-site radiant exposure, whereas the TRIADE R61 trial deliberately varied optical parameters and found optical-parameter-dependent, bidirectional BOLD power responses. The historical record also leaves biological mechanism unresolved: mitochondrial/redox, neurovascular, glial-inflammatory, network-mediated, and diffuse or systemic pathways remain plausible at different levels of evidence, and a distributed physiological response does not by itself identify where the effect begins. These observations support a constrained historical inference: dose, depth, and delivery site are biological variables, not merely device specifications. We distinguish focal-local, diffuse/systemic, and local-stimulation/network-mediated accounts of action and identify prospective tests that can discriminate among them. The next phase of dtPBM development should prioritize indications in which optical access, target engagement, and a disease-relevant network or biomarker can be specified prospectively rather than inferred after a clinical outcome.

candidates.title: A Clinical Insight into Von Hippel-Lindau Syndrome: Diagnostic Challenges.
candidates.abstract: Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) syndrome is a rare hereditary disorder characterised by the development of multiple benign and malignant tumours across various organs. Caused by mutations in the VHL tumour suppressor gene, it presents a wide range of clinical manifestations, including retinal haemangioblastomas, central nervous system tumours, renal cell carcinoma, pancreatic lesions, and phaeochromocytomas. This report describes the case of a 35-year-old woman who presented with visual impairment and abdominal masses. Imaging revealed typical VHL manifestations, including bilateral renal lesions and pancreatic involvement. Genetic testing confirmed the diagnosis. The patient underwent staged partial nephrectomies, with histopathology confirming clear cell renal cell carcinoma in both kidneys. This case highlights the importance of recognising the variable clinical and radiological presentations of VHL syndrome. Early diagnosis and multidisciplinary management are essential to reduce morbidity and mortality. Increased awareness and regular surveillance are critical for timely detection and intervention in patients with VHL syndrome.

candidates.title: Pegvisomant in severe, treatment-resistant thyroid eye disease: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Teprotumumab, a monoclonal antibody against the IGF1 receptor, has proven effective in the treatment of thyroid eye disease (TED). Pegvisomant reduces IGF1 levels through selective inhibition of growth hormone receptors. Here, we present a hypothesis-generating case of a 69-year-old patient with progressive TED. Pegvisomant 20 mg was administered daily for 90 days. IGF1 levels declined and remained low-normal during treatment. Clinical activity scores and VISA (vision, inflammation, strabismus and appearance) scores improved rapidly. MRI assessment showed that water content of both extraocular muscles and orbital connective tissue decreased after treatment. 99mTc-DTPA SPECT confirmed the decrease in disease activity. Further studies may confirm the efficacy of pegvisomant in TED. A 69-year-old female patient with severe, active thyroid eye disease (TED) – a condition linked to Graves’ disease where the body’s immune system attacks tissues around the eyes – presented with bulging eyes (proptosis), double vision, eye redness, swelling and reduced visual sharpness.Prior treatments with standard therapies for TED, including intravenous steroid courses, radiation therapy targeting the orbit (eye socket) and the biological drug rituximab, failed to achieve improvement. TED progresses in part because proteins called IGF1 receptors on the surface of eye-socket tissues are overactivated. The researchers hypothesized that using pegvisomant, which is a medication typically used for acromegaly (hormone imbalance) that lowers insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1) levels in the blood, would reduce activation of these receptors and ease eye inflammation.The patient received a daily 20 mg injection of pegvisomant for 90 days. Symptom improvement The patient experienced a rapid reduction in eye pain, redness and swelling, alongside marked improvement in visual sharpness and colour vision within 8 weeks.MRI and imaging results Orbital MRI and nuclear imaging showed a distinct drop in tissue inflammation and fluid accumulation (oedema) in the muscles around the eye.Proptosis and double vision Eye bulging and double vision did not significantly change during the trial.Safety Pegvisomant was well tolerated with no reported side effects, and her blood sugar and liver function remained stable. Blood IGF1 levels dropped as expected and returned to normal after treatment ended. Pegvisomant rapidly reduced eye inflammation and improved vision in a patient whose TED had resisted standard therapies. However, because this was a single case study, the delayed effects from previous treatments cannot be entirely ruled out. Further clinical trials are needed to determine if pegvisomant is effective at higher doses or when given earlier in the disease course.

candidates.title: Polygenic risk score identifies alternative etiologies in misdiagnosed cases of primary adrenal insufficiency.
candidates.abstract: Primary adrenal insufficiency (PAI) is commonly caused by autoimmunity in adults, known as autoimmune Addison's disease (AAD). Autoantibodies against 21-hydroxylase are a hallmark of AAD but are absent in some patients diagnosed with AAD, posing a challenge to their clinical management. We tested a polygenic risk score for AAD (PRS14AAD) to prioritize seronegative patients for etiologic reevaluation. The PRS14AAD was calculated in patients diagnosed with AAD but lacking 21-hydroxylase autoantibodies (n = 124). Patients with low (n = 35) or high (n = 10) genetic susceptibility to AAD underwent clinical re-evaluation and whole-genome sequencing. Of the 34 patients with low PRS14AAD, 14 (41%) were re-diagnosed with non-autoimmune adrenal insufficiency, whereas no alternative etiologies were identified in patients with high PRS14AAD. The low PRS group included six patients (17%) with confirmed monogenic PAI and eight patients (23%) with adrenal insufficiency due to either tuberculosis or non-primary causes. Notably, four of the six confirmed monogenic cases developed PAI in adulthood, consistent with late-onset disease caused by hypomorphic variants. Additionally, seven patients (20%) carried genetic variants suspected of causing monogenic disease. These findings support considering genetic evaluation in patients with seronegative PAI, regardless of the age at diagnosis.

candidates.title: Medullary thyroid carcinoma with pheochromocytoma and cystic parathyroid degeneration in a ret-negative patient: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2A (MEN2A) is a rare autosomal dominant hereditary cancer syndrome, predominantly caused by mutations of the RET proto-oncogene on chromosome 10q11.2. It typically presents with medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), pheochromocytoma, and primary hyperparathyroidism. Cases with a MEN2A phenotype but negative RET testing are uncommon, posing challenges for diagnosis and patient management. We report the case of a 63-year-old female who was diagnosed with MTC and pheochromocytoma. and cystic parathyroid gland. Genetic workup was negative for RET proto-oncogene mutations but positive for a heterozygous variant in the TMEM127 tumor suppressor gene. MEN2A is associated with pathogenic germline variants in the RET proto-oncogene in approximately 95-99% of cases. Our patient, however, exhibited a MEN2A-like clinical phenotype in the absence of an identifiable RET mutation, with a pathogenic TMEM127 variant instead. Although TMEM127 is an established susceptibility gene for pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma, its association with the broader MEN2A phenotype remains unclear. This unusual genotype-phenotype discordance raises important questions regarding the potential role of alternative genetic pathways in MEN2-like syndromes and creates uncertainty regarding postoperative surveillance and the appropriate extent of screening and genetic counseling for family members. Our case represents an unusual scenario where the patient presents with a clinical phenotype of MEN2A but is RET negative and positive heterozygous for a variant in the TMEM127. This atypical genetic finding introduces complexities in determining the appropriate follow-up protocol and the scope of familial screening necessary.

candidates.title: Establishing standardized evaluation protocols for peptide-target interaction prediction: the PTI-TAPE consensus framework eDelphi.
candidates.abstract: Computational peptide-target interaction (PTI) prediction has advanced rapidly as a tool for drug discovery, yet the field lacks agreed evaluation standards. Discrepancies in metrics, negative sampling strategies, and dataset construction across publications currently render cross-study comparisons methodologically intractable, ultimately impeding the clinical translation of therapeutic peptides. To resolve this, we present PTI-TAPE (Peptide-Target Interaction-Tasks Assessing Peptide Engagement), a standardised benchmarking framework developed via a structured three-round eDelphi consensus study with 15 international experts spanning computational biology, machine learning, and regulatory science. Operating under a robust consensus threshold (>80% agreement), the panel established 26 definitive standards across eight domains, governed by the new STRIDE (Standardisation, Transparency, Representativeness, Integration, Discovery, Evidence) framework. Key outcomes include mandating specific primary metrics for affinity and structure, enforcing a tiered negative sampling hierarchy that prioritizes experimental non-binders, and requiring mandatory temporal dataset splits. By providing a unified reporting checklist, benchmark specifications, and a biennial governance structure, PTI-TAPE ensures reproducible evaluation and fair method comparison, bridging the gap between computational PTI predictions and genuine therapeutic benefit.

candidates.title: GNAI2 activating variants and MAGIS syndrome: long-term endocrine and growth outcome.
candidates.abstract: Germline activating variants in the GNAI2 gene have recently been associated with MAGIS syndrome, characterized by midline malformations of the brain, anterior pituitary gland dysfunction, growth retardation, immunodysregulation, and skeletal defects. However, the full phenotypic spectrum, particularly regarding endocrine dysfunction, remains incompletely defined. We report on a 9.5-year-old male presenting with MAGIS syndrome due to a de novo GNAI2 (NM_002070.4):c.544A>C, p.(Thr182Pro) variant. He initially presented at 17 months with short stature and hypopituitarism. Pituitary MRI confirmed anterior pituitary hypoplasia with thin stalk and normal posterior pituitary. Long-term follow-up revealed suboptimal response to recombinant growth hormone therapy with persistent low IGF-1, profound prolactin deficiency, and evolving gonadotropin deficiency. He also had delayed developmental milestones, recurrent infections, chronic diarrhea, subclinical hypothyroidism, and skeletal abnormalities. Immunological evaluation showed low T-cell counts, inadequate antibody responses and no overt autoimmune features apart from infantile atopic dermatitis. This report details the longitudinal clinical, endocrine, and growth data in a patient with MAGIS syndrome harboring a GNAI2 p.Thr182Pro variant. It highlights the suboptimal growth response to GH with fluctuating height velocity and the development of additional endocrine abnormalities such as prolactin, thyroid dysfunction and suspected gonadotropin deficiency. Detailed phenotypic characterization in such cases is crucial for understanding this complex genetic disorder.

candidates.title: Acute cerebellitis as a post-infectious complication of primary varicella in an immunocompetent young adult: A case report.
candidates.abstract: Acute cerebellitis is a well-documented neurological sequela of primary varicella-zoster virus (VZV) infection. Although frequently reported in children, this complication remains uncommon in adults and may present diagnostic difficulties, especially when neuroimaging studies are normal. A previously healthy, immunocompetent 20-year-old man was admitted with a four-day history of progressive gait instability and imbalance. Nine days prior to admission, he had developed a generalized vesicular rash consistent with primary varicella, initially involving the trunk and subsequently spreading to the face and extremities. He also reported occipital and frontal headaches, undocumented fever during the active phase of the rash, and postprandial nausea with vomiting. Neurological examination revealed intact consciousness, normal cranial nerve function, truncal ataxia, a wide-based gait, impaired tandem gait, and inability to maintain balance during Romberg testing even with eyes open. No appendicular ataxia was detected. Laboratory studies showed a normal complete blood count and an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 13 mm/hour. Brain computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging revealed no acute pathological findings. Cerebrospinal fluid polymerase chain reaction (PCR) was positive for VZV. Intravenous acyclovir (750 mg three times daily) was initiated, with subsequent gradual clinical improvement. Post-varicella cerebellitis should be included in the differential diagnosis of adults presenting with acute truncal ataxia following recent primary varicella infection, even when neuroimaging is normal. Cerebrospinal fluid VZV PCR is a valuable diagnostic aid, and early antiviral therapy may be associated with favorable outcomes.

candidates.title: GClnc1 as an emerging oncogenic regulator with mechanistic insights and clinical implications in human cancers.
candidates.abstract: Gastric cancer-related long non-coding RNA1 (GClnc1) is an emerging oncogenic regulator in multiple malignancies, including gastric, colorectal, ovarian, and bladder cancers, as well as osteosarcoma. It promotes proliferation, inhibits apoptosis, and enhances drug resistance and metastasis. Mechanistically, GClnc1 dysregulates key cancer-related regulators and pathways, such as p53, MYC, NF-κB, and the SIRT3/SOD2 axis. Clinically, GClnc1 shows diagnostic and prognostic potential across cancers, with aberrant expression in tissues and altered circulating levels. Notably, exosomal GClnc1 serves as a circulating biomarker for early gastric cancer detection and predicts response to fluorouracil-based chemotherapy. This review summarizes current evidence on GClnc1's regulatory mechanisms and discusses its translational applications. GClnc1 may serve as a multi-cancer biomarker and a promising therapeutic target.
